newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM's Mt Isa copper output slumps in Q4.
newsitem.headline: MIM's Mt Isa copper output slumps in Q4.

text.p: Copper concentrate production from MIM Holdings Ltd's Mount Isa operations fell sharply in the three months to June 30, MIM's quarterly report on Monday showed.
Mount Isa copper concentrate production fell to 1,143 tonnes in the fourth quarter from 21,749 tonnes in the same quarter a year earlier.
This took total Mount Isa-sourced copper concentration for the year to June 30 to 9,159 tonnes from 24,244 tonnes in the 1995/96 year.

Copper concentrate production at Mount Isa from purchased concentrates fell to 1,212 tonnes in the quarter from 2,442 a year earlier. Total non-Mount Isa sourced concentrate production for the year fell to 1,892 tonnes from 7,997 tonnes.

Refined copper production from MIM's Townsville refinery fell to 42,621 tonnes in the quarter from 51,528 tonnes in the same quarter a year earlier. Annual Townsville copper production rose however to 179,677 tonnes from 175,755 tonnes in 1995/96.
MIM said that ore production was affected by low haulage fleet availability in the quarter.

"Townsville refinery production in the fourth quarter was affected by the shortage of anode that resulted from the February/March rebrick of the Mount Isa Isamelt furnace, but was offset by good operating performances during May and June," MIM said.
It said a new anode casting wheel was being installed at Mount Isa during August as part of the copper smelter expansion.
"While this will affect anode production in the first quarter of 1997/98, the smelter will continue to produce copper and full year production will not be affected."
Work progressed on the Townsville refinery expansion with no impact on production, MIM said.
The planned period of suspended anode production at Mount Isa during August would allow work on the refinery expansion to be carried out without overall cathode production being disrupted.
Zinc, lead and silver output for the quarter were consistent with the previously announced revised mining strategy, MIM said.

Coal production at MIM's Oaky Creek mine rose to 876,110 tonnes in the fourth quarter from 763,539 tonnes in the same quarter a year earlier, taking annual production to 3.06 million tonnes from 2.73 million tonnes.

Construction at MIM's 50 percent-owned Alumbrera copper-gold project in Argentina was 96 percent complete and the first concentrate production was due to enter the concentrator pipeline during the first quarter of 1997/98.
Alumbrera is owned 25 percent by North Ltd and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd.
